title: The fleet Live Activity's content state
description: What the AgentPod hub puts in a fleet Live Activity push's `aps.content-state`: one card for a reader's whole fleet, what needs them and what is happening now. This is the producer's shape, as strict as AgentPod's zod `FleetContentState` (packages/contract/src/fleet-live.ts): no key the app has never heard of may leave the hub, and every bound is applied before a push. Readers are lenient: SuperMessage's Swift decoder (`FleetActivityAttributes.ContentState`) ignores unknown keys, reads a missing optional key as none, skips an agent or option it cannot read, and reads an unknown agent state as `active`. A reader checks against this schema only to test what it is sent, never to refuse a push. Keys are camelCase; times are Unix seconds. The text here (agent names, the step, a decision's question and options) reaches Apple in plaintext, by operator decision of 2026-09-29.

agents.description: At most three: needs_you first, then working, then the most recent.

mxid.description: The agent's Matrix id; the app keys its cached avatar by it.

phase.description: Where a working turn is on the card's track. Only while state is working.

step.description: The step it is on, or how its turn ended. At most 60 characters (code points).

completed.description: Tool calls done. The hub omits it, and total, while a working turn has made none.

since.description: Unix seconds: when the turn started (also for a finished row), or the last activity.

endedAt.description: Unix seconds: when the turn finished. Only while state is done or failed.

id.description: What the app sends back to answer: a permission option's name, or a gate option's id.

kind.description: `attention` (2026-11-08) is a card waiting on a person; it is sent with no options. A reader that predates a kind may read it as a permission, which is why a new kind offers nothing it could not send.

options.description: Inline options only: at most two. Never an "always" grant.
